title: "Other ecosystem roles" is read in its broadest sense, reaching contributors who merely support an actor
content:
A.1.5.5.0.4.2 instructs facilitators on the scope of the prohibition: "The phrase 'other ecosystem roles' is read in its broadest sense to mean the totality of roles that are formally defined in the Atlas with a function in the Sky ecosystem." Its non-exhaustive list runs Alignment Conserver, Governance Process Support Ecosystem Actor, Active or Incubating Ecosystem Actor, Agent Advisor, Arranger — "and the contributors supporting these aforementioned actors."

The last clause is the expansive one. It extends the ban past role holders to the people working for them, meaning an individual contributor on an Ecosystem Actor team cannot also be an Aligned Delegate. Combined with A.1.5.5.0.4.3's rule that a role "need not be compensated or full-time to be regulated," the reachable population is large: anyone doing any amount of work, paid or not, for any Atlas-defined actor.

The interpretive instruction is itself notable. Most of the Atlas's supporting apparatus exists to *narrow* meaning — Element Annotations "bound the semantic meaning" of problematic terms. Here a Tenet does the opposite, deliberately widening a phrase. That is coherent under the framework's logic on prohibitions: for a rule whose purpose is preventing conflict of interest, a narrow reading creates exploitable gaps, and gap-exploitation is the letter-of-the-rule behaviour the Atlas treats as misalignment.

The Atlas records its own doubt about the resulting breadth. NR-3 asks whether team contributors should be covered at all, noting that "quality contributors are a scarce resource," that "the decentralized work paradigm encourages having several part-time jobs," and that cross-team experience "might arguably enhance ecosystem intelligence" — the framework's own stated goal. The rule as written resolves that tension in favour of conflict prevention, but flags it as unsettled.
description: A.1.5.5.0.4.2 enumerates Governance Process Support EAs, Active or Incubating EAs, Agent Advisors, Arrangers and their supporting contributors as roles that trigger the single-role prohibition.
